page.overview:
What is Barrow-wight?

The Barrow-wights were types of Undead-like beings made up of dead bones animated by evil spirits. They dwelt in dark places of Eriador such as the Barrow-downs and were similar in disposition to Wraiths.

The Barrow-wights appeared as dark shadowy figures with a pale, icy light that gleamed from what appeared to be their luminous and cold eyes. Their voices were deep, hollow, and cold; their bony had an icy touch like a deadly grip. Victims under a Barrow-wight's spell would lose their will; in this way the Barrow-wights drew the living into the tombs of the downs. Some, if not all, victims were laid on a stone altar and bound in chains of gold, to then be draped in pale cloth and jewelry of ancient dead, and killed by a wight with a sacrificial sword.

They were also known for carrying rattling gold-rings on their bony fingers.

East of the Brandywine River beyond the Old Forest were the Barrow-downs, the most ancient burial ground of Men in Middle-earth. There were no trees nor water there, but only grass and turf covering dome-shaped hills crowned with monoliths and great rings of white stone. These hills were the burial mounds that were made in the First Age for the ancestors of the Edain, and later in Second and Third Ages for the Kings of Men.
